body:
Landing, integration and install methods. Who may act: CLAUDE.md "Commit and push" and greg-decisions.

LANDING TRAIN (Termal::Fable2, 2026-09-30, refined by Termal::Opus2 and agreed). When origin/master no longer matches the reviewed base, CLAUDE.md says to "coordinate integration and validate and review the resulting input before publishing". Landing changes one at a time sends every other change back to a new gate and pair; instead the integration owner runs a train:
1. Each author finishes on its own base: own full gate, own review pair with no Medium or higher, Lows filed, a commit with explicit paths, and a handoff (hash, gate run, diff sha256, review ids). Authors do not move base, merge or rebase for their own round.
2. The owner builds the train as ONE uncommitted merge: `git merge --no-commit --no-ff` of all handed-off commits at once, in an integration worktree on origin/master. No intermediate merge commits, no rebase, no amend. Nothing is committed before it is gated and reviewed.
3. One full gate on that uncommitted tree, then one read-only review pair (Codex and Claude), told which commits it holds and that each was reviewed on its base; its job is the integration. With no Medium or higher, the merge is committed, and master is fast-forwarded to it and pushed: one build, one install, one restart signal.
4. A change that fails the train's gate or draws a Medium is dropped: `git merge --abort`, then the same merge without it, and it returns to its author. A failure is diagnosed, never retried on unchanged input.
5. Git refuses a multi-head merge that needs manual resolution, so a change that conflicts textually with another cannot ride with it. The later one in the announced order waits for the next train, or its author resolves on the new master in its own round.
6. Each carried item records the train commit, its gate run and its review ids as its exact-tree evidence.
7. Authority text does not ride a train as-is. Its final-diff audit must name the fingerprint of the gated input, which for a train is the integrated tree. It lands alone, or its audit is made on the train's tree.
A change not handed off when the train leaves takes the next one.

AUTHORITY-TEXT AUDIT. Checked-in text: .claude/commands/review-changes.md Step 7 (who audits, what counts as a changed passage, when it passes). Before a landing of authority text (any repository instruction or command file that grants or limits commit, push, tracker or approval authority), the coordinator reads the FINAL frozen diff line by line against the recorded sentences, and notes on the item which mailbox message gives each landed passage's wording and which concurs on it. A passage that no message quotes whole is concurred on, word for word, before the freeze, or taken out. Proposals in messages are not the check: wording is amended in rounds and composed passages slip through.
Method: reading alone is not enough. Compare by script: the whitespace-normalised landed text against the recorded sentences as exact strings, plus a word-level diff. Why: on Engram's first freeze three reviewers stated 'verified verbatim' and all missed lost backticks; the script caught it.
Origin: TermAl 60a56a9 (2026-09-29) landed two composed passages whose wording was concurred only after landing; Greg accepted the deviation ('akceptuje'); Engram found two in ff305a6. Adopted by both coordinators 2026-09-29. Engram's text: commit 778e59654c3edde5b53075bc8dc2906385504fff; TermAl's mirror (w-881b50cb66d1) is Step 7.

BUILD AND INSTALL
- The integration owner installs the binary from the exact gated tree, outside any gate window, renaming the running binary aside and recording its hash (CLAUDE.md). Swap order: live-workarounds, "Install swap".
- Never build in place under the live server (Greg via Fable, 2026-09-03): it runs from the master checkout and serves ui/dist from disk. Never run `npm run build` in ui/, or `cargo build --release`, in a dirty or unverified master tree. To check a UI build, use `npx tsc --noEmit` and Vitest, or `npx vite build --outDir ../target/ui-dist-check`.
- Exact-commit release binary (Fable, 2026-09-05): build from a clean export, never a dirty checkout: `git archive <commit> | tar -x -C target/release-clean-<sha>/src`, then in that directory `cargo build --release --locked --target-dir ../target`. The CLI has no --help: `<exe> --help` prints "fatal: unknown argument" and exits 1, which proves it loads. Never point a test run at ~/.termal.

UI/DIST DEPLOY (Fable, 2026-09-05, corrected 2026-09-10). Who: the integration owner, for the latest landed UI (greg-decisions); other deploys need Greg's word.
- TermAl serves the prebuilt ui/dist, not a Vite dev server. Editing ui/src changes nothing in the running app, and green tsc and Vitest prove nothing about what the user sees. Always rebuild (deploy the current UI by the authorised build-and-copy procedure) before asking the user to verify a UI change; three debugging rounds were once lost on a five-week-old bundle.
- The hazard is the live directory being built into or emptied. `npm run build` in ui/ empties it: vite.config.ts sets no outDir, and Vite empties an outDir inside its root (2026-09-10). State the condition that must never hold, not the command never to run.
- Build completely elsewhere (a separate outDir, or a clean export under target/ with ui/ and scripts/, since vite.config.ts imports ../scripts/vitest-resource-preflight.mjs; junction node_modules). Copy the new hashed assets into ui/dist first and index.html last. Leave the old assets for clients holding the old index.html. Never remove and then move the directory. Copy-over is not atomic and not zero-downtime; do not call it a safe swap.
- Verify delivery, not the build: diff -rq <build> ui/dist; GET / and read which asset the served index names; GET that asset and grep it for an identifier the change introduces, with a control identifier that predates the change; compare its SHA256 with the file on disk. Delivery is not interaction: whether the feature works needs its own observation.
- Tell the user to reload. A cached index.html still names the old asset; if a report says the feature is still missing, check the reload before hunting a defect.

DONE ONLY AFTER LANDING (Termal::Fable2, 2026-10-03). A holder runs `done` on its item only AFTER the integration owner reports the landed master commit, and cites that commit. Before landing it holds the claim, with evaluation, commit and handoff complete. Why: w-e16e7268155a was sealed done before landing, then train 26's integration pair found an in-scope Medium (w-116927ba1140), leaving a "done" item whose code was not on master. The decision there (note 6c458110 on w-e16) is to keep the seal, fix under the new item, and land the original commit together with the fix in one train. A parent with live child claims cannot be completed, so finish the children first.
